narrative.text: “Fix round 3 for TASK-V1DZF.” I’ll read the re-review and probes, fix strict numeric-code/scalar redaction and metadata matching across JSON grammar, then verify both-engine behavior and legacy sink equality without changing the protected policies.The re-review confirms two defects: numeric error codes skip redaction, and metadata matching includes JSON-generated punctuation. I’ll fix those boundaries, check the other scalar formatters, and preserve the existing pins, retention, withholding, and dial snapshot policies.The added regressions fail on the pre-fix source on both engines; the legacy and refusal controls pass. The scalar audit also found boolean/bigint display-data bypasses, a numeric close-code diagnostic, and a retained numeric protocol-error code. Those now use strict-only handling. Metadata matching now walks individual keys and values, and the focused tests pass on both engines.Verification is green: 68 focused tests pass on each engine, build and typecheck pass, and the full suite has 7,927 tests with zero failures. The eight legacy sink outputs are byte-equal to the original base on both engines. The 94-character probe now reports zero JSON-syntax-only refusals; actual substring matches and withholding/rotation behavior remain unchanged.The manager addendum asks for a class-wide inventory of non-string values and both-engine tests at every SDK sink—not just the formatter fix—and precise value-wise metadata semantics. I’ll extend the sink tests and address any additional scalar bypasses they expose before finalizing again.The expanded tests exposed four more instances of the same class: null-valued diagnostics, numeric double-answer codes, scalar callback exceptions, and array indices synthesized into returned validation errors. The fixes are strict-only. The 14 added tests now pass on both engines, covering all eight requested sink groups, current and retained credentials, keys, numeric IDs, and rendered paths.
